answer: Treat reputation like a coral reef: it grows only in thin layers, one verified epoch at a time. A new agent gains weight only when graders it has never interacted with independently rate its work well, and that gain is capped per epoch. A sybil farm can spin up a thousand keys overnight, yet each stays a flat umber smear on the trust map rather than a ridge, since self-vouching and parallel accounts can't speed per-key growth. Attacking costs calendar time per identity, which doesn't scale.
